title: Make the agent run typecheck and lint without being asked
goal: The tests are green but typecheck and lint fail. Write a context file with the verification commands and a definition of done, then give the agent a task that never mentions them. It should run them and fix what they find.
setup_cmd: D=~/fm-ex/ex-2-3-feedback-loop; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo "Already set up at $D. Run: cd $D (or delete it first to start over)."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-2-3-feedback-loop/starter "$D" && cd "$D" && npm i; fi

starter_prompts.claude: Add a truncate(text, max) function to src/text.js. Text longer than max is cut so the result is exactly max characters and ends with a single … character (the ellipsis counts towards max). Shorter text is returned unchanged. Add a test in test/app.test.js.
starter_prompts.codex: Add a truncate(text, max) function to src/text.js. Text longer than max is cut so the result is exactly max characters and ends with a single … character (the ellipsis counts towards max). Shorter text is returned unchanged. Add a test in test/app.test.js.

solution_notes: AGENTS.md names the exact commands in order (npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm test) and says why: type and lint errors do not fail the tests in this repo.
The definition of done is a set of exit codes, including 'for files you did not touch', which is what makes the agent fix the errors that were already there.
The rules say what not to do (no @ts-ignore, no any, no editing checks), because an agent told to get green will otherwise weaken the check.

CLAUDE.md is a single @AGENTS.md line. The task prompt never mentions typecheck or lint. That is the point: the context file carries the loop. The solution also implements truncate, and `.verify/truncate.test.js` checks it.
